prerequisites: Mathematical support in differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the main scientific-technological knowledge necessary for their comprehensive development, promoting their interaction in the field of Electrical Engineering.
Know the necessary technical specifications of electrical equipment with which a desirable maintenance can be achieved for the proper functioning of industrial facilities.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and concise exposition.
Ability to distribute resources and time and implement them in real situations.
Capacity for the use of scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work collaboratively and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.

syllabus_topics: ELECTRICITY: GENERAL CONCEPTS. Magnitudes and elements in electrical engineering. Review of electricity. Electrical circuits. Potential difference. Current intensity. Receivers. Generators. Power. Energy. Ohm's Law. Resistance. Self-induction. Capacitor. Standardization. Symbolism. Electrical circuits
CIRCUIT ANALYSIS. Kirchhoff's Laws. Mesh current method. Application of matrix algebra to circuit analysis. Thevenin's Theorem. Star-delta transformation theorem.

ALTERNATING CURRENT. Production of a sinusoidal alternating current. Elements and parameters of a periodic wave: Effective value, average value, frequency, phase shift. Resistive, inductive, and capacitive circuit. Impedance. Complex notation in alternating current circuits. Active, apparent, and reactive power. Power factor improvement.

POLYPHASE ALTERNATING CURRENT SYSTEMS. Three-phase circuits. Advantages of using three-phase systems. Star and delta connection of sources. Phase and line voltages and currents: relationship between them in balanced systems. Receiver connection. Power in balanced three-phase systems.

ELECTRICAL ENERGY SYSTEMS. Introduction to the generation, transmission, and distribution of electrical energy. Single-phase and three-phase distribution. Types of power plants. Substations. Introduction to low voltage installations. Electrical equipment
teaching_methods: Participatory lecture method for theory classes
Audiovisual aids (transparency projector, multimedia programs, videos)
Guided visit to electrical facilities (Campus electrical installations, Hydroelectric power plant, Solar farm, Wind farm, Electrical substation, etc.)
assessment_rules: The final grade will be 85% from the exam and 15% from continuous assessment. To pass the course, both parts must be successfully completed. The written test at the end of the semester consists of a theoretical part (multiple-choice and short-answer questions) and a problem-solving part. The theoretical part accounts for 20-40% of the written test, and the problem-solving part accounts for 60-80% of the written test.
